- When sentiment is consistently low or negative (≤ 0.00) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75.00), model often overshoots in the next 5–10 days; cap forecast at +2–5% above peak or use moving average of prior 5 days.
- If sentiment is positive but price history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 72.00), model overreacts; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day.
- When sentiment is neutral or weak (0.00–0.30), model tends to forecast higher than true; use 3-day rolling median as baseline for correction.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below 70.00 after a high, model often fails to adjust; apply a “floor” correction at 68.00–69.50 if sentiment is flat or negative.
- If sentiment is rising (e.g., >0.50) but price is falling, model may misread trend; use sentiment as a multiplier (e.g., 0.8x) to dampen forecast if price is trending down.
